ordered_diagnoses: Necrotizing fasciitis due to Bacillus cereus

facts.raw_span: A female infant with history of acute lymphoblastic leukemia
was admitted for reinduction chemotherapy
Seventeen days after her last day of chemotherapy, while neutropenic, she became febrile
Patient had an indwelling catheter
Several vesicles with an erythematous base were observed on the lower back and left thigh
Hematoxylin-eosin stain showed focal epidermal and subepidermal necrosis with numerous filamentous bacilli with septa
Gram stain revealed numerous gram-variable rods in the necrotic epidermis and dermis
Periodic acid-Schiff staining was negative for fungal elements
PCR testing for herpes simplex virus (HSV) and varicella zoster virus (VZV) were negative
CT scan with contrast of thorax and brain showed lesions in the liver and brain

Hematoxylin-eosin stain showed focal epidermal and subepidermal necrosis with numerous filamentous bacilli with septa

Periodic acid-Schiff staining was negative for fungal elements

concepts.why: The presence of filamentous bacilli with septa and gram-variable rods in the necrotic epidermis and dermis, as seen in the hematoxylin-eosin stain and Gram stain, respectively, is consistent with Bacillus cereus infection.
The patient's neutropenic state, indwelling catheter, and presence of vesicles with an erythematous base are risk factors for Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection.
The presence of an indwelling catheter and the development of fever and vesicles are consistent with a catheter-related bloodstream infection.
The patient's neutropenic state and fever are consistent with neutropenic fever.
The patient's history of acute lymphoblastic leukemia and the presence of lesions in the brain are consistent with leukemic meningitis.
The patient's history of acute lymphoblastic leukemia and the presence of lesions in the liver are consistent with hepatic involvement of leukemia.
The presence of lesions in the liver and brain, as seen on the CT scan, is consistent with disseminated intravascular coagulation.
The patient's fever, neutropenia, and presence of vesicles with an erythematous base are consistent with sepsis.

rationales.F09: The negative PCR results for HSV and VZV make C05 less likely.
rationales.F10: The presence of lesions in the liver and brain on CT scan could be indicative of leukemic meningitis or hepatic involvement of leukemia, making C05 and C06 more likely.
